363040.title: Mészáros–Setiabrata–St. Dizier's coefficient-sum conjecture for Grothendieck polynomials
363040.literal_statement:
Fix $w\in S_n$ and write

$$
\mathfrak{G}_w(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{Z}^n} C_{w\alpha}x^\alpha.
$$

Let $\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w^{\mathrm{top}}(x))$ denote the exponents of monomials of highest degree in $\mathfrak{G}_w(x)$, and order exponents componentwise. **Mészáros–Setiabrata–St. Dizier's coefficient-sum conjecture.** For any $\beta\in\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak{G}_w^{\mathrm{top}}(x))$, one has

$$
\sum_{\alpha\leq\beta} C_{w\alpha}=1.
$$

This conjecture concerns the coefficients below each top-degree monomial and is part of the support and coefficient properties studied in the paper; its general resolution is not supplied in the stated context.
363040.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: The zero-one factorization proof in source Section 4 gives the sum by disjoint-variable factors. Arbitrary permutations need not admit those factors; proving the general signed lower-ideal sum is missing. No transfer from the restricted theorem.
363040.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363214.title: The one-branch-point conjecture for crossing-free Hubbard trees
363214.literal_statement: Let a Hubbard tree be a forward-invariant tree associated with a quadratic polynomial, and call it **crossing-free** when the relevant tree dynamics satisfy the source's crossing-free condition. A branch point is a point of the tree whose removal leaves more than two components. **The one-branch-point conjecture.** If the Hubbard tree is crossing-free, then there is only one branch point. The preceding lemmas in the source establish that branch points are pre-periodic and that every pre-fixed branch point is fixed in the crossing-free case, but the supplied text does not state whether this claim is proved or remains open.
363214.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: Crossing-free is an external semantic condition. Preperiodicity plus the fixed-prefixed lemma does not exclude multiple periodic branch orbits. Need actual crossing-free model and a global branch-orbit exclusion; body not reviewed.
363214.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363366.title: The e-positivity conjecture for hat-chains
363366.literal_statement:
A **hat-chain** is the graph constructed by joining the indicated complete graphs and paths, as in the hat-chain construction preceding the conjecture; an expression is **e-positive** when its chromatic symmetric function has a nonnegative expansion in the elementary symmetric-function basis.

**Hat-chain e-positivity conjecture.** Every hat-chain is $e$-positive.

Hat-chains form a family of conjoined graphs, and the conjecture asserts a uniform positivity property for their chromatic symmetric functions. The supplied text does not indicate whether this assertion has been proved or disproved.
363366.review_depth: Source construction and resolution report; companion selected theorem/proof excerpts
363366.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: Latest source explicitly credits Tom–Vailaya. Hat chains are adjacent cycle chains with the stated end paths; no new credit. Companion arXiv:2410.21762 downloaded and selected cycle/attachment proof text reviewed. Journal and all version comparison not completed; exclusion is supported by source report, not claimed exhaustive proof audit.
363366.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363413.title: The specific sequence irregularity strength conjecture
363413.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph without a component isomorphic to $K_2$. For each $1\le i\le\Delta(G)$, let $n_i$ be the number of vertices of degree $i$, and define

$$
M_G=\max\left\{\left\lceil\sqrt[i]{n_i}\right\rceil:1\le i\le\Delta(G)\right\}.
$$
 The **specific sequence irregularity strength conjecture.** The specific sequence irregularity strength of $G$ is equal to $M_G$.

Specific sequence irregularity strength asks for the existence of an ordering of $E(G)$ for which an edge coloring induces distinct color sequences at all vertices. The paper presents this as a weaker conjecture after refuting the general version, and no resolution is supplied here.
363413.review_depth: Primary definitions, Theorem 1 proof and Conjecture 5; 2013 journal Section 3 proof excerpts
363413.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: See ORDINARY-ATTEMPTS.md. Need globally orderable compatible distinguishing words with exactly M_G colors, or a genuine nondegenerate witness against every edge order. No such object or theorem proved.
363413.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363458.title: Jayanthan–A R conjecture on linear type binomial edge ideals
363458.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $S=\mathbb{K}[x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_n]$, and let

$$
J_G=(x_i y_j-x_j y_i\mid i<j,\ \{i,j\}\in E(G))\subset S
$$

be its binomial edge ideal. An ideal $I\subset A$ is **of linear type** when its symmetric algebra is naturally isomorphic to its Rees algebra, $\operatorname{Sym}(I)\cong\mathcal{R}(I)$. **Jayanthan–A R conjecture.** If $G$ is a tree or a unicyclic graph, then $J_G$ is of linear type. This conjecture proposes a combinatorial characterization of a class of binomial edge ideals analogous to the known characterization for ordinary edge ideals; its resolution status is not specified in the source.
363458.review_depth: Primary definitions and complete Proposition 5.3 proof
363458.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: C4 with one pendant edge at each cycle vertex is connected unicyclic and is its own induced C4,1. Proposition 5.3 gives non-linear type by an explicit quadratic relation outside the linear relation ideal. Exact literal universal claim is already publicly false; no new credit.
363458.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363506.title: Yip's lower-bound conjecture for the Tesler flow polytope
363506.literal_statement:
Let $\bm{N}=(1,1,\ldots,1,-n)$, and let $K_n(\bm{N})$ denote the number of lattice points of the corresponding Tesler flow polytope. Recall that $f_n\sim e^{1/2}\cdot n^{n-2}$ is the number of forests with vertex set $[n]$, equivalently the number of lattice points of the classical permutahedron.

**Yip's conjecture.** For $\bm{N}=(1,1,\ldots,1,-n)$, we have

$$
K_n(\bm{N})\geq f_n.
$$

Yip proposed this as a weaker statement than the conjecture that the Tesler polytope $\mathcal{F}_n(\bm{1})$ projects to the permutahedron. The bound would compare the lattice-point count of the Tesler flow polytope with the number of forests on $[n]$; the source provides no resolution of this conjecture.
363506.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: A directed increasing forest is only a subclass of labeled forests, so sending edges toward larger vertices does not yield the required injection of all forests into nonnegative Tesler flows. Need an injective encoding preserving every hook sum 1; no full mechanism established.
363506.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363511.title: Nilpotency conjecture for the Collatz adjacency submatrices
363511.literal_statement:
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\longrightarrow\mathbb{N}$ be the shortcut Collatz function, and let $A$ be the infinite matrix with entries

$$
a_{ij}=\delta_{f(i),j}.
$$

For $n\geqslant 3$, let $C_n$ be the $(n-2)$-by-$(n-2)$ submatrix indexed by $\{3,\ldots,n\}$, with entries $c_{ij}=a_{ij}$. A matrix is **nilpotent** if some positive power of it is zero.

**Nilpotency conjecture for the Collatz adjacency submatrices.** If $n\geqslant 3$, then the matrix $C_n$ is nilpotent.

The paper presents this matrix statement as a matricial formulation equivalent to the aperiodic Collatz conjecture. Since the underlying Collatz assertion remains unresolved, this claim is open.
363511.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: For a finite functional digraph, adjacency nilpotency is equivalent to absence of a directed cycle: a cycle supplies nonzero walks of every length, and an acyclic graph has no walk of length its vertex count. Applying this for every n is exactly exclusion of all nontrivial finite Collatz cycles, not a new route.
363511.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363544.title: The diameter conjecture for Cayley graphs generated by $p$-singular elements
363544.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group and let $p\in\pi(G)$ be a prime. Let $\Omega_p(G)$ be the set of $p$-singular elements of $G$, and let

$$
\Gamma_p(G):=\operatorname{Cay}(G,\Omega_p(G)).
$$

For a graph, write $\operatorname{diam}(\Gamma_p(G))$ for its diameter, and write $|G|_p$ for the $p$-part of $|G|$.

**Diameter conjecture.** The diameter satisfies

$$
\operatorname{diam}(\Gamma_p(G))\leq |G|_p.
$$

The paper notes that this would extend the corresponding theorem for $p$-solvable groups to all finite groups, conditional on Brauer's $k(B)$-conjecture for principal blocks. The supplied text does not establish the conjecture in general.
363544.review_depth: Primary definition, Conjecture 4.2 and nearby proof
363544.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: The reference note saying refuted belongs to the energy bound, not Conjecture 4.2. Source proves p-solvable case and explains principal-block Brauer condition. Neither energy counterexamples nor a p-solvable theorem refutes/proves the exact general diameter bound.
363544.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363575.title: Extension of the double-dimer result to CP hyperbolic triangulations
363575.literal_statement: Let $G$ be a CP hyperbolic triangulation, without necessarily assuming bounded degree or nonamenability. **Extension conjecture.** The statements of Theorems $\mathrm{thm:main0}$ and $\mathrm{thm:main}$ hold for CP hyperbolic triangulations. The authors expect that the bounded-degree and nonamenability assumptions can be removed, leaving CP hyperbolicity as the relevant condition; this extension is posed as an open question.
363575.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: Removing bounded degree/nonamenability requires new uniform control of double-dimer limits and boundary behavior. Literal theorem references are not expanded in the record; body definitions and the full limiting theorem remain unread.
363575.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363589.title: Monotonicity conjecture for metered parking functions
363589.literal_statement:
Let $m,n$ be positive integers, and let $\mathrm{mpf}_{m,n}(t)$ denote the number of $t$-metered $(m,n)$-parking functions. **Monotonicity conjecture.** If $t_1<t_2$, then

$$
\mathrm{mpf}_{m,n}(t_2)\leq \mathrm{mpf}_{m,n}(t_1).
$$

This conjectures that the number of metered parking functions is nonincreasing as the number of meters varies, despite the lack of set containment between the corresponding sets. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture is treated as open.
363589.review_depth: Primary Definition 1.1, examples and proof excerpts; journal Conjecture 1 and surrounding proof; 2026 companion fiber lemmas and proofs
363589.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: See ORDINARY-ATTEMPTS.md. Pointwise preference containment fails. Outcome feasibility nests but fiber weights increase in the opposite direction. No weighted injection or sum inequality for all m,n,t is proved.
363589.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363609.title: Infinite log-monotonicity conjecture for transposed Boros-Moll sequences
363609.literal_statement: Let $d_\ell(m)$ be the coefficient of $x^\ell$ in the Boros-Moll polynomial $P_m(x)$. For a sequence $\{a_i\}_{i\geq 0}$, let $\mathcal{R}\{a_i\}_{i\geq 0}=\{a_{i+1}/a_i\}_{i\geq 0}$. A sequence is **infinitely log-monotonic** when every iterate has alternating log-concavity and log-convexity as specified by the paper's definition. **Infinite log-monotonicity conjecture.** The transposed Boros-Moll sequence $\{d_\ell(m)\}_{m\geq\ell}$ is infinitely log-monotonic for $\ell=0$. The sequence $\{d_\ell(m+1)/d_\ell(m)\}_{m\geq\ell}$ is infinite log-monotonic for each $\ell\geq 1$. The $ll=0$ sequence is known to be log-convex and ratio log-concave, but the asserted infinite behavior remains open.
363609.review_depth: Statement, current metadata and completed family notes
363609.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: Infinite alternation requires all ratio iterates for both l=0 and every l>=1. Prior completed r116 addresses different finite derivative/ratio inequalities (363608), not this exact endpoint. The record solved note quotes unimodality of a different orientation and cannot settle this statement.
363609.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363641.title: K_l-critical graph conjecture
363641.literal_statement: For an integer $\ell\geq 2$, call a graph $G$ **$K_{\ell}$-critical** if it contains a copy of $K_{\ell}$, is vertex-critical, and removing the vertex set of any copy of $K_{\ell}$ reduces its chromatic number by $\ell$. **$K_{\ell}$-critical graph conjecture.** If $G$ is $K_{\ell}$-critical for some $\ell\geq 2$, then $G$ is a complete graph. This conjecture generalizes the double-critical graph conjecture and is presented as an open strengthening motivated by counterexamples to the Erdős–Lovász–Tihany conjecture.
363641.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: At ell=2 the condition includes the double-critical graph conjecture. A clique-removal coloring of G minus Q need not extend consistently to force every pair in G adjacent. No general extension lemma or in-scope counterexample.
363641.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363666.title: The non-generation conjecture for off-diagonal cycles in deleted graph products
363666.literal_statement:
Let $K$ be a graph, and let $K^{\square\underline 2}$ denote its deleted Cartesian square. The cycles under consideration include off-diagonal cycles, symmetrized cycles, and boundaries in this graph.

**Off-diagonal cycle conjecture.** In $K^{\square\underline 2}$, no off-diagonal cycle is a sum of boundaries and symmetrized cycles.

This is presented as an analogue of the corresponding assertion for $K^{\square 2}$, with the deleted Cartesian square in place of the Cartesian square. The source gives no resolution status.
363666.review_depth: Primary Russian Sections 1.7 and 1.9 definitions and Conjecture 1.9.3; selected surrounding bodies
363666.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: Off-diagonal cycle is the explicit staircase on a simple cycle; symmetrized cycles in source mean a×C+C×a, not arbitrary z+swap(z). Passing to full Cartesian product loses the deleted-cell obstruction. A planar winding argument would need a drawing-independent cocycle vanishing on all disjoint-edge square boundaries in arbitrary graphs. Not established; no finite witness.
363666.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363715.title: Stability of eigenmaps for random averaging Laplacians
363715.literal_statement:
Let $g(x)$ be a smooth sampling density on $\mathbb{R}$, and let random averaging Laplacians be constructed from points sampled according to $g$. Define

$$
\mathcal{L}_{(g)}f:=-2\frac{g'}{g}f'-f”.
$$

**Stability conjecture.** Eigenmaps of the random averaging Laplacians give numerically stable locally uniform approximations to the corresponding eigenmap of $\mathcal{L}_{(g)}$. This predicts locally uniform spectral stability for sampling from smooth distributions; the half-line case requires suitable boundary conditions, and a related multidimensional case is discussed in the paper.
363715.review_depth: Statement, current version metadata and completed family notes
363715.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: The exact bandwidth regime, eigenvalue isolation, boundary conditions and probabilistic convergence mode are absent from the abbreviated literal record. Prior r116 nearby eigenmap review is an analytic hold; no new uniform spectral theorem.
363715.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363885.title: The planar graph equilibrium conjecture
363885.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a strongly connected planar graph, and let $g$ denote its undirected girth. A **static equilibrium** is an equilibrium of the static type, while a **$2$-chase equilibrium** and a **WT equilibrium** are the cycle-based equilibrium types defined in the paper. **Planar graph equilibrium conjecture.** All strongly connected planar graphs with

$$
g\geq 4
$$

have either a static equilibrium, a $2$-chase equilibrium, or a WT equilibrium. The conjecture extends the paper's result for strongly connected outerplanar graphs and is motivated by constructions of strongly connected graphs of girth $5$ without cycle-based equilibria, all of which are non-planar; its resolution for general planar graphs remains open.
363885.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: A planar girth-4 orientation could only refute the claim after ruling out static, 2-chase and WT equilibria under the actual game semantics. Strong connectivity and lack of a short directed cycle are insufficient. No full in-scope construction.
363885.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363917.title: Chromatic-number bound for intersections of general matroids
363917.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}=\{\mathcal{M}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{M}_k\}\in\mathcal{D}^k$, where $\mathcal{D}$ is the class of matroids under consideration, and let $\bigcap\mathcal{L}$ denote their intersection. **Chromatic intersection conjecture.** One has

$$
\chi\left(\bigcap\mathcal{L}\right)\le k\max_{1\le i\le k}\chi(\mathcal{M}_i).
$$

The surrounding discussion concerns general matroids; the corresponding list-coloring estimate with factor $k$ is proved, while this chromatic formulation is posed as a conjecture.
363917.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: Source gives list bound (2k-1) times max individual chromatic number for general matroids, and factor k for partition matroids. The list-vs-ordinary bound k chi(intersection) cannot be substituted for k max chi(M_i). Full factor-k general bound missing.
363917.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363919.title: k-minus-one ratio conjecture for matroid polytopes
363919.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{L}\in\mathcal{D}^k$ be a family of $k$ matroids, and let $R(\mathcal{L})$ and $P(\bigcap\mathcal{L})$ denote the polytopes defined in the source. **Polytope ratio conjecture.** One has

$$
R(\mathcal{L}):P\left(\bigcap\mathcal{L}\right)\le k-1.
$$

The source states this as equivalent to the weighted matching-cover conjecture. The bound is established for partition matroids, while the general case remains open.
363919.review_depth: Primary definitions and Conjecture 1.8 equivalence discussion
363919.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: Polytope ratio generalizes weighted matching-cover/Ryser-type assertion. k=2 integrality or proved partition/small-k cases do not imply all k. The omitted lower bound on k is not used as an endpoint counterexample. No full general proof.
363919.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

363989.title: The EKR conjecture for induced subgraphs of perfect matchings
363989.literal_statement:
Let $M_n$ be the graph consisting of $n$ pairwise disjoint copies of $K_2$, and let $4\mathcal{H}^{(p,s)}(n)4$ be the family of induced subgraphs of $M_n$ consisting of $p$ disjoint edges and $s$ isolated vertices, where $s,p$ are non-negative integers and $1\leq 2p+s\leq n$. A family of members of $4\mathcal{H}^{(p,s)}(n)4$ is intersecting if any two of its members have a common vertex.

**EKR conjecture.** $4\mathcal{H}^{(p,s)}(n)4$ is EKR: every intersecting subfamily has size at most the size of a star, with equality attained by a family consisting of all members containing a fixed vertex of $M_n$.

This conjecture extends two distinct Erdős–Ko–Rado-type theorems to families of induced subgraphs of perfect matchings. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
363989.review_depth: Original definitions and theorem bodies; Nagy entire short proof
363989.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: Nagy arXiv:2407.17455 Theorem 4 is verbatim equivalent for nonnegative p,s and 1<=2p+s<=n. Vertex subsets and their induced graphs correspond bijectively. Double-cycle quasi-interval proof handles both parities of s and gives star density (2p+s)/(2n). Public since July 2024; journal 2025 metadata independently found. Zero credit.
363989.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

364010.title: Involution-equivalence conjecture for cycle-free d-partitions of K_{2d}
364010.literal_statement: Let $K_{2d}$ be the complete graph on $2d$ vertices. A **cycle-free $d$-partition** is a cycle-free edge $d$-partition of $K_{2d}$, and two such partitions are **involution equivalent** if one can be obtained from the other by a finite sequence of the involutions $(x,y,z)$, where $1\leq x<y<z\leq 2d$. **Involution-equivalence conjecture.** Any two cycle-free $d$-partitions of $K_{2d}$ are involution equivalent. The conjecture is the purely combinatorial form of the uniqueness, up to a constant, of the map $det^{S^2}$; its resolution is not given in the source.
364010.review_depth: Primary definitions and Conjecture 3.2; selected main theorem/appendix excerpts
364010.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: Actual triangle involution is nonlocal. Ordinary tree edge exchange need not be an allowed triangle involution preserving all d trees. Source twin-star reduction and d<=4 cases leave transitivity for arbitrary d unproved; no parameter instance credited.
364010.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result

364122.title: The NP-completeness of 2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT for binary matroids
364122.literal_statement: A binary matroid is a matroid representable over the two-element field. The 2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT problem asks whether a matroid has a circuit containing two specified elements. **2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT conjecture.** 2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT is NP-complete for binary matroids. The source explains that this conjecture, together with a reduction from 2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT to the complement of $\operatorname{EqualitySY}_0$, would imply the binary-matroid part of the EqualitySY coNP-completeness conjecture; the complexity of 2-SPANNING-CIRCUIT for binary matroids remains open.
364122.review_depth: Primary Conjecture 14.8 and surrounding reduction discussion
364122.ordinary_attempt_and_residual: For literal two prescribed elements and an explicit representation, the classical common-circuit/component test is polynomial via basis fundamental-circuit components. This is routine matroid connectivity, not a substantive discovery. Membership in P alone does not unconditionally negate NP-completeness (would require P!=NP); no refutation claimed. Source intended scope needs reconciliation.
364122.formalization: not dispatched; no source-qualified new ordinary result
